title: Minimum Difference Between Largest and Smallest Value in Three Moves
statement:
You get an integer array `nums`. A move replaces a single element with any integer you like, and you may make up to three moves (possibly fewer, possibly on the same element).

Return the smallest possible gap between the maximum and the minimum element of `nums` once your moves are done.
notes:
## Intuition

Overwriting an element is as good as deleting it: you can always set it to some value already inside the remaining range. So the question becomes which three elements to delete. Deleting anything from the middle never shrinks the range, so the best three to delete are some mix of the smallest and largest values: `k` from the bottom and `3 - k` from the top, for `k` from 0 to 3. Trying every subset of three would also work, but costs O(n³ · n).

## Approach

1. Let `n` be the length. With four or fewer values, three moves can make everything equal, so return 0.
2. Sort `nums` ascending.
3. For each `removeLow` from 0 to 3, set `removeHigh = 3 - removeLow`. The survivors run from index `removeLow` to index `n - 1 - removeHigh`, so their range is `gap`.
4. Keep the smallest `gap` in `best` and return it.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [5, 3, 2, 4]` has only 4 values, so `n <= 4` and the answer is `0` right away: change three of them to equal the fourth.

Example 2 shows the loop at work: sorted `nums = [0, 1, 5, 10, 14]` and `n = 5`, so each split keeps two neighbours. `removeLow = 0` keeps `[0, 1]` (gap 1), `removeLow = 1` keeps `[1, 5]` (gap 4), `removeLow = 2` keeps `[5, 10]` (gap 5) and `removeLow = 3` keeps `[10, 14]` (gap 4). `best` ends at `1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort; the scan checks only four windows.
- Space: O(1) beyond the sort, which works in place.

## Pitfalls

- Handle `n <= 4` first, otherwise the indices `n - 1 - removeHigh` can fall before `removeLow`.
- JavaScript's default `sort` compares strings; pass `(a, b) => a - b`.
- Only removing from the ends matters, but both ends must be tried in every split, not just "remove the three largest".

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | number of values |
| `best` | smallest gap found so far |
| `removeLow` | how many of the smallest values are overwritten |
| `removeHigh` | how many of the largest values are overwritten |
| `gap` | range of the values that are kept |

narration.2: Remember how many values there are.
narration.3: With four or fewer values, three moves can make them all equal.
narration.4: So the gap can be brought down to zero.
narration.7: Sort so the smallest and largest values sit at the two ends.
narration.8: No split has been tried yet.
narration.10: Try overwriting 0, 1, 2 or 3 of the smallest values...
narration.11: ...and the rest of the three moves on the largest values.
narration.12: The kept values span from index removeLow to index n - 1 - removeHigh.
narration.16: Return the best of the four splits.
